'''Tsuchimikado Harutake''' (土御門 晴雄, Tsuchimikado Harutake)<ref group="note">The Wakatsugi Family Documents contain a signature "晴雄" with the reading "タケ" for "雄" annotated. Another document bears the name "はれ雄."</ref> was a noble of the late {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. He was the de facto final head of the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|ja|土御門家|lt=Tsuchimikado family}} and the head of {{ill|Onmyōdō|en|Onmyōdō|qid=Q1340540|lt=Onmyōdō}}. His court Rank was {{ill|Senior Third Rank|ja|正三位}}, and he served as {{ill|Q11547969|ja|民部卿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minister of Popular Affairs|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11547969}}.

== Career ==
Harutake was born on {{ill|June 28|en|June 28|qid=Q2660|lt=June 28}}, {{ill|1827|en|1827|qid=Q7008|lt=1827}} ({{ill|Bunsei|en|Bunsei|qid=Q1327119|lt=Bunsei}} 10) to {{ill|Tsuchimikado Harechika|ja|土御門晴親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Harunaga|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11423479}} and his consort Keijunin. At age six, he was granted the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位上|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade}}, and in {{ill|1839|en|1839|qid=Q7616|lt=1839}}, upon coming of age, he held the Rank of {{ill|Dazai Gon no Daibu|ja|大膳大夫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daizen Daibu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大膳職|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11438575}}. In {{ill|1842|en|1842|qid=Q7625|lt=1842}}, he was appointed head of the {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽寮}}.

During his career, Harutake also served as {{ill|Hyōefu|ja|右兵衛佐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Right Guard Officer|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 兵衛府|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11393702}} and reached the Rank of {{ill|Senior Third Rank|ja|正三位}}. In {{ill|1868|en|1868|qid=Q7717|lt=1868}}, he resigned as Minister of Popular Affairs.

{{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|Tokugawa shogunate}}'s {{ill|Tenmongata|en|Tenmongata|qid=Q11442660|lt=Tenmonkata}}, consolidating control over calendar and astronomical affairs under the {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽寮}}. Despite advocating for a revised {{ill|Lunisolar calendar|en|Lunisolar calendar|qid=Q194235|lt=Lunisolar calendar}}, his proposals were delayed due to the new government's lack of interest.

Harutake passed away at 43 in {{ill|1869|en|1869|qid=Q7720|lt=1869}}. His posthumous name was Yangō-in-den Shōsanmi Abe Harutake-kyō, and his remains rest at {{ill|Bairin-ji|ja|梅林寺 (曖昧さ回避)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Baijinji Temple|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q803940}}.

== Succession ==
With the death of Harutake's son Harutsuna in {{ill|1868|en|1868|qid=Q7717|lt=1868}}, the family's leadership passed to his adopted son, {{ill|Tsuchimikado Harenaga|ja|土御門晴榮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuchimikado Haruyasu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17315120}}. However, by {{ill|1870|en|1870|qid=Q7741|lt=1870}}, the {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽寮}} was disbanded by the new government. By {{ill|1873|en|1873|qid=Q7757|lt=1873}}, the {{ill|Gregorian calendar|en|Gregorian calendar|qid=Q12138|lt=Gregorian calendar}} replaced the lunisolar system.
